data.title: ITAT Mumbai stays ₹8,520 crore tax demand on Singapore govt over gains
data.description:
The Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT), Mumbai, has stayed the recovery of tax demands totalling around ₹8,520 crore raised on the Government of Singapore. The Income Tax Department had denied it an exemption on capital gains earned from investments in India under the India-Singapore tax treaty.
 
The demands relate to three assessment years: ₹3,345.95 crore for 2022-23, ₹2,057.15 crore for 2023-24 and ₹3,116.96 crore for 2024-25. The stay will remain in force for 180 days from October 23, 2026 (the date of the order), or until the disposal of the appeals, whichever is earlier.
 
The dispute centres on Article 22 of the India-Singapore Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement (DTAA). Article 22(2)(c) exempts the government of a contracting state from tax in the other state on dividends, interest and any other income or gains derived from transactions that are not pursuant to the conduct of commercial activities. The term “Government” under the treaty includes the Government of Singapore and certain specified entities.
 
 
The Government of Singapore, which invests in India as part of its global investment activities through its fund manager GIC Private Limited, claimed that its capital gains, dividends and interest income were exempt under the treaty. The assessing officer accepted the exemption for dividends and interest but denied it for capital gains, holding that the gains arose from commercial activities.
 
Singapore has been claiming the exemption since assessment year 2010-11. The department accepted the claim in scrutiny assessments for 2010-11 and 2011-12 and while processing returns under Section 143(1) of the Income-tax Act up to 2020-21. A similar addition was made for assessment year 2021-22, but the dispute was resolved in Singapore’s favour under the Mutual Agreement Procedure (MAP), under which the competent authorities of the two countries discuss and resolve disputes relating to the interpretation or application of tax treaties. The Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT) later deleted the addition. MAP proceedings for the three years currently under dispute are also underway.
 
Seeking the stay, Singapore argued that its exemption claim had been consistently accepted in earlier years and that the facts of the present cases were similar to those resolved in its favour under MAP for 2021-22. It also pointed to its status as a sovereign government and said that around 17 per cent of the demand for assessment year 2022-23 had already been recovered through refund adjustment and tax deducted at source. It further contended that even under domestic law, a sovereign entity is not a “person” under Section 2(31) of the Income-tax Act and is therefore not taxable.
 
The department opposed the stay and argued that Singapore should be directed to pay 20 per cent of the outstanding demand.
 
The tribunal observed that the applicant is a sovereign government with which India has longstanding diplomatic and economic ties and that it cannot be treated on a par with an ordinary taxpayer. It noted that the exemption claim had been accepted by the department up to 2020-21 and by the competent authorities under MAP for 2021-22, and that MAP proceedings for the disputed years are already under active consideration. It also referred to a recent coordinate Bench decision in the Fullerton Financial Holdings case, which held that income of the Government of Singapore is not taxable under the relevant treaty provisions.
 
"Thus, upon due consideration of the prima facie case, the balance of convenience, and the fact that the assessee’s applications for resolution of disputes under MAP are under consideration… we are inclined to grant a stay on recovery of demand…," the tribunal said.
 
It directed that the appeals for all three assessment years be heard together on December 28, 2026. The tribunal clarified that its observations were made only in the context of the stay applications and would have no bearing on the final decision on merits.
 
“The ruling shows that a consistent history of accepted claims, together with a live MAP process, can outweigh routine pre-deposit demands, which should reassure sovereign and government investors. It also signals to tax officers that reopening a long-settled treaty position, especially one already resolved under MAP, will face close scrutiny at the recovery stage. Other foreign investors should be cautious about relying on it, since the Tribunal gave significant weight to the applicant’s sovereign status,” said Amit Kumar Maheshwari, managing partner, AKM Global.

data.title: UK, EU seek closer ties a decade after Brexit as Burnham visits Brussels
data.description:
A decade after the people of Britain voted to leave the European Union, top EU officials are meeting with Prime Minister Andy Burnham on Friday, looking to mend more fences, and just perhaps, to pave the way for them to get back together.

Burnham is scheduled to hold just under an hour of talks in Brussels with European Council President Antonio Costa and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen. Then they'll all meet in a plenary session with UK government ministers and European commissioners.

Burnham has described the rare EU-UK summit - only the second since Britain became the first country to leave the world's biggest trading bloc - as a step toward undoing a decade of damage caused by the divorce.

 

"The Brexit we were given has not worked. We have lost more than we gained," he said this week.

Burnham has said all options should be on the table for future relations, including rejoining the now-27-nation bloc.

But he's stressed that reversing Brexit is just one possible outcome, and far from imminent. It would need the backing not just of British voters, but the unanimous support of a mistrustful EU. Still, he has broken a long political code of silence on the option of rejoining.

Burnham says closer ties will ease the cost of living

Ahead of the meeting, von der Leyen said she wanted it to be "a summit of ambition and concrete results. More opportunities for young people. Easier agrifood trade. And a stronger cooperation on economic security." Burnham pitched the package of agreements expected to be agreed Friday as a way of "cutting costs, keeping prices down in the supermarkets and creating opportunities for young people." He said "a closer partnership with Europe is good for working people, good for Britain and good for Europe." The deals are set to include an agreement for up to 100,000 young adults from Britain to live and work in EU countries for up to three years, and the same number of Europeans to come to the UK.

There will also be an emissions trading agreement and a deal to remove checks on food and agricultural products that will make things cheaper and easier for British exporters to Europe. Burnham said Friday the deals could add 0.5 per cent to Britain's economy - he'd previously set it at 0.4 per cent.

But nothing in UK-EU relations is ever quick or simple. An EU official said the package is contingent on the two sides reaching agreement on university tuition fees in the next six months. EU negotiators want European students to pay domestic fees if they study in Britain, something the UK has resisted. The official said negotiations had not been easy but they sensed good will to resolve the issue.

The official was designated to brief reporters about the summit but only on condition that they not be named.

Talks are also continuing on Britain's desire to have access to the bloc's "made in Europe" rules for manufacturing.

Critics say the deals are a betrayal of Brexit

To get the deals, the UK must accept some EU rules and standards that it has no role in setting. Supporters of Brexit say that undermines Britain's independence.

"I'm afraid that the great Brexit debate has just started again," Reform UK leader Nigel Farage told the BBC. He said "it's perfectly clear that this very, very soon becomes a debate about: do we rejoin or do we stay out?" The war in Ukraine, and the UK's military strength, are drawing the two back together, and the summit provides the EU with an opportunity to discuss stronger cooperation on security and defence, as well as efforts to restrict irregular migration.

"Our security and prosperity are closely intertwined, making a strong partnership between us essential," Costa said ahead of the meeting. "By deepening our cooperation, we can strengthen our ability to address the challenges of our time, strengthen our resilience and promote stability in Europe and beyond." Nevertheless, feelings remain raw, and EU officials have been reluctant to encourage talk of the UK rejoining. They are weary from the shifting demands of seven British prime ministers over the last decade and want real clarity about the country's intentions.

Ireland's ambassador in London, Sonja Hyland, said that when Britain voted for Brexit, "there was a lack of clarity as to exactly what that meant." If Britain wants to reopen negotiations, she said, it must "make a clear decision as to what it wants.

data.title: SC upholds Karnataka HC ruling allowing bike taxis, dismisses appeal
data.description:
The Supreme Court on Friday dismissed the Karnataka government's appeal against a Karnataka High Court judgment permitting motorcycle owners and aggregators to operate bike-taxi services in the state, paving the way for their continued operation.
 
A Bench of Justices Satish Chandra Sharma and N Kotiswar Singh upheld the High Court's January 23, 2026, judgment, which had directed the state authorities to consider applications for registering motorcycles as transport vehicles and issuing permits for their use as bike taxis.
 
During the pronouncement of the verdict, Justice Sharma recalled an interaction with young women who had visited his office and used bike taxis to commute.
 
 
"I asked them, how do you come to my office? They said on a motorbike because they do not have the money to hire a cab. I asked them, why don't you take an auto? They said, 'Sir, it is five times (the fare)'," the judge said.
 
The dispute arose after a single-judge Bench of the Karnataka High Court ordered a halt to bike-taxi services until the state government formulated a policy regulating their operations.
 
The order was challenged by aggregators Ola, Uber and Rapido, along with motorcycle owners and the Bike Taxi Welfare Association.
 
On January 23, a Division Bench comprising then Chief Justice Vibhu Bakhru and Justice C M Joshi allowed their appeals and lifted the restrictions. It held that motorcycles could be registered as transport vehicles and operated as contract carriages. The state government could prescribe regulatory conditions for their operation but could not deny permits solely on the ground that the vehicles were motorcycles.
 
The Karnataka government subsequently moved the Supreme Court, citing concerns over passenger safety, insurance coverage and the absence of adequate regulatory safeguards.
 
Five associations representing auto and taxi drivers also challenged the High Court's decision, arguing that allowing bike taxis without imposing comparable regulatory obligations would put existing transport operators at a disadvantage.
 
During the hearings, the Supreme Court questioned the state's objections, including its concerns over traffic congestion. It observed that motorcycles occupied less road space than cars and also highlighted the affordability of bike-taxi services.
 
The state government argued that motorcycles and motor cabs were distinct categories under the Motor Vehicles Act and that the existing aggregator rules did not specifically provide for bike taxis. It also contended that aggregators had no automatic right to operate such services, relying on a 2019 expert committee report that examined safety, congestion and pollution-related concerns.
 
Karnataka told the court that it was willing to consider allowing bike taxis in other parts of the state but remained opposed to their operation in Bengaluru.
 
The aggregators, however, submitted that nearly 4 lakh passengers had benefited from bike-taxi services in Karnataka. They relied on an earlier High Court ruling that had not been challenged and government notifications issued in 2004 and 2024.
 
In response to a query from the Bench, the Centre also confirmed that motorcycles could be used as taxis under its notifications.
 
After considering the submissions, the Supreme Court dismissed the state's appeal, leaving the High Court's directions in place.
 
Reacting to the verdict, Pavan Guntupalli, co-founder of Rapido, said, “We welcome today’s decision by the Hon’ble Supreme Court. It brings important clarity to the bike taxi category in Karnataka and marks a landmark moment for the sector in India."
 
In a press release, he stated that over the years, bike taxis have demonstrated their value by helping commuters navigate congested cities, strengthening first- and last-mile connectivity, and creating flexible earning opportunities for captains.
 
"The verdict recognises the role the category already plays on the ground and provides a stronger foundation for its continued growth and integration into the mobility ecosystem," he said.
 
He emphasised that for Rapido, the verdict is more than a legal outcome.
 
"It is an affirmation of something we have consistently believed in: that India needs mobility solutions designed around the way people actually travel," he said.
 
"Two-wheelers are among the most widely owned and accessible mobility assets in the country, and enabling people to use them productively can create meaningful value for commuters, captains and cities alike. We look forward to working with the Government of Karnataka to take the category into its next phase, safe, responsible, regulated and at scale,” he added.

data.title: Alkemi Growth Capital plans $125-150 million third fund launch in 2027
data.description:
Healthcare- and wellness-focused investment firm Alkemi Growth Capital is planning to launch its third fund, with a corpus of $125-150 million, in 2027. With fresh funds, the venture capital firm is looking to expand its bets on healthcare innovation, preventive medicine and medical deep-tech startups.
 
In a conversation with Business Standard, Alka Goel, the firm’s founding partner, said, “We are planning to launch our third fund, targeting $125 million to $150 million, between March and June 2027.” The proposed fund will follow its first two funds of $40 million and $75 million.
 
Goel said Alkemi has already begun informal conversations with existing limited partners (LPs), although formal fundraising discussions have yet to begin. Alkemi has previously raised capital from the International Finance Corporation (IFC), the Teachers' Retirement System of the State of Illinois (TRS), and the Small Industries Development Bank of India (Sidbi).
 
 
Alkemi has so far invested in 14 companies through its ongoing $75 million fund and expects to back another four over the next six months. The firm typically invests in four to six companies annually, with initial cheque sizes ranging between ₹20 crore and ₹30 crore.
 
Some of Alkemi’s portfolio companies include Redcliffe Labs in diagnostics, Medvital in medical devices, Datar Cancer Genetics in IVD deep-tech, Medulance in emergency medical response, Alphadroid in autonomous mobility robots, Leumas in physical AI for pharma manufacturing, and Jagruti in the mental health and rehabilitation segment, among others.
 
With its third fund, Alkemi is also looking to increase its exposure to deep-tech startups operating in healthcare. "We have already invested in two or three companies in deep-tech. This has happened in the last one-and-a-half years. We will definitely see more," Goel said. With its third fund, the average ticket size is also likely to increase to ₹25-40 crore.
 
Beyond deep-tech, preventive healthcare is a major investment theme for the firm. Goel said rising disposable incomes and greater consumer awareness are driving spending on preventive wellness, diagnostics, wearables, nutrition and fitness. "Healthcare is forever. There is no limit to innovation in healthcare," she said, adding that the opportunity extends beyond hospitals to pharmaceuticals, medical devices, diagnostics and preventive health.

data.title: Uttar Pradesh's microfinance portfolio grows 6% to ₹34,446 crore in Sept
data.description:
Uttar Pradesh's microfinance outstanding portfolio grew 6 per cent year-on-year to ₹ 34,446 crore at the end of September 2026, signalling a recovery in the sector after a period of contraction and rising delinquencies.
 
The portfolio stood at around ₹ 32,500 crore at the end of September 2025. This marks a turnaround from the 20 per cent contraction recorded in the corresponding quarter of FY26, when outstanding microfinance loans fell to around ₹ 32,500 crore from nearly ₹ 40,000 crore a year earlier.
 
According to Sudhir Sinha, chief executive officer of the Uttar Pradesh Microfinance Association (UPMA), the sector is gradually returning to growth after a period of relative decline and rising delinquencies.
 
 
“We must empower microfinance institutions (MFIs) to develop a sustainable and future-ready model. While technology is essential, we must ensure that human beings are not left behind,” he said.
 
With nearly 9 million borrowers, Uttar Pradesh is India's second-largest microfinance market, accounting for 12 per cent of the country's outstanding portfolio. Non-banking financial company-microfinance institutions (NBFC-MFIs) account for the largest share of lending in the state at 51 per cent, followed by private banks, small finance banks (SFBs) and other NBFCs.
 
During the July-September quarter of FY27, microfinance lending in the state grew by more than 3 per cent to ₹ 7,520 crore from ₹ 7,250 crore in the corresponding quarter of FY26.
 
The average ticket size (ATS) of microfinance loans in Uttar Pradesh also increased 9 per cent, from ₹ 56,501 in September 2025 to ₹ 61,765 in September 2026.
 
Addressing the ninth Microfinance State Annual Conference 2026, organised by UPMA in Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh State Transformation Commission (STC) Chief Executive Officer Manoj Kumar Singh urged MFIs to prepare a roadmap for reducing lending rates. He also stressed the need to strengthen the rural economy and promote entrepreneurship to expand employment opportunities in the state.
 
The conference deliberated on restructuring the microfinance sector in response to emerging socio-economic needs and building a more inclusive ecosystem.
 
M Rajeshwar Rao, former deputy governor of the Reserve Bank of India, highlighted responsible lending, customer protection, fair interest rates and institutional transparency as essential to the sector's long-term sustainability.

data.title: UPI MDR debate sparks fresh calls for revision of AePS interchange fees
data.description:
The move to price the Unified Payments Interface (UPI) through a merchant discount rate (MDR) – albeit in abeyance for now - has triggered a fresh demand to revisit the pricing on the Aadhaar Enabled Payment System (AePS).
 
AePS is a bank-led payment system developed by the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) which allows for basic banking transactions for customers using their Aadhaar number and biometric authentication, allowing for online interoperable financial inclusion transaction at Points of Sale (PoS, or micro-ATM) through business correspondents (BCs) of any bank. Cash-in and cash-out is the mainstay of BCs.
 
Pricing on AePS has remained static for nearly a decade at 0.5 per cent of the ticket size or Rs 15, whichever is lower. This affects the channel’s financial viability, a key cog in the financial inclusion and direct benefits transfers (DBT) and Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY).
 
“AePS serves remote villages where ATM deployment is commercially unviable. Sustainable economics for touch points is essential to ensure continued availability of assisted banking services in underserved geographies,” said Anand Kumar Bajaj, founder-managing director and chief executive officer (CEO), PayNearby.
 
The Reserve Bank of India’s (RBI’s) October monthly bulletin puts the number of AePS transactions at 999.48 lakh for the month of August with a transaction value of Rs 24,747 crore. For the entirety of FY26, these numbers stood at 12,126.36 lakh and Rs 3.22 trillion.
 
The RBI has strengthened onboarding, Know-your-customer (KYC), and monitoring requirements for AePs outlets which has increased compliance and technology investment for acquiring banks and service providers. With growing dependence on AePS for DBT withdrawals, pension payments and basic banking services, the sustainability of the last-mile cash-distribution network is becoming increasingly critical.
 
“The current interchange framework creates increasing pressure on the commercial viability of business correspondents and AePS touchpoint operators, with implications for agent retention and the continued availability of assisted banking services, particularly in rural and underserved areas,” Bajaj said.
 
“With the decision to price UPI (though it has not kicked in), there is increased urgency to look at AePS charges too. The channel too has to be priced correctly to make it a viable financial inclusion too. More so for DBT and PMJDY beneficiaries,” noted Dharanidhar Tripathy, CEO of the Business Correspondent Resource Council. He also pointed out that compared to AePS, the ATM ecosystem has witnessed periodic revisions to its interchange and customer charge framework. The interchange fee is what one bank pays another when its debit card is used at the latter’s ATM.
 
The RBI has permitted ATM networks to determine interchange while continuing to prescribe customer protection through mandatory free transactions and a ceiling on customer charges. Customers continue to enjoy five free transactions at their own-bank ATMs and three/five free transactions at other-bank ATMs (metro/non-metro respectively), subject to a maximum customer charge of ₹23 per transaction beyond the free entitlement, effective 1 May 2025. In effect, the gap between the ATM interchange for cash withdrawals and AePs pricing has widened to Rs 4. This, even as cash-in, cash-out transactions remain the mainstay of BC earnings, accounting for more than 60 per cent of their income.
 
“A periodic review mechanism linked to changes in operating cost, similar to the ATM ecosystem will AePS,” said an an industry source. He pointed to the deliberations between the RBI and the Confederation of ATM Industry for linking the ATM interchange fee to the wholesale price index that measures wholesale inflation.
 
According to Sumita Kale, CEO and senior fellow, Indicus Foundation, AePS pricing should be seen in the larger context of the National Strategy for Financial Inclusion (NSFI): 2025-30. It had highlighted the importance of BCs’ remuneration, their training or expanding the scope of the products and services provided by them. “Since 2014, we at the Indicus Centre for Financial Inclusion have been making a case for improved metrics to track financial inclusion beyond the number of bank accounts and business correspondents, etc, to include data on active/dormant agents, usage of accounts, the quality of service/transactions, etc. Ideally, data on each indicator should be released, as this can help service providers and India’s central and state governments focus their efforts more effectively”, Kale said.
                                         Behind the call for AEPS pricing review
  • Pricing on AePS has remained static for nearly a decade at 0.5 per cent of the ticket size or Rs 15, whichever is lower
  • This affects the channel’s financial viability, a key cog in DBT and PMJDY
  • A periodic review mechanism linked to changes in operating cost, similar to the ATM ecosystem is now being demanded for AePS.
  • RBI’s October monthly bulletin puts the number of AePS transactions at 999.48 lakh for the month of August with transaction value at Rs 24,747 crore. For FY26, these numbers stood at 12,126.36 lakh and Rs 3.22 trillion

data.title: Rajasthan govt targets energy surplus, pushes power storage projects
data.description:
The state government is working to transform Rajasthan into an energy-surplus state, Energy Minister Hiralal Nagar said, stressing the need to expedite power generation projects and strengthen the electricity infrastructure.
 
Nagar was recently reviewing power availability in the state, preparations for uninterrupted electricity supply during the upcoming Rabi season, daytime power supply to farmers in two blocks, and the progress of schemes such as PM-KUSUM and PM-Surya Ghar.
 
With renewable energy accounting for an increasing share of the state's power mix, the minister emphasised the need to accelerate Battery Energy Storage (BES) projects. He said battery storage was crucial for effectively utilising solar and wind energy and maintaining grid stability during peak hours.
 
 
He directed the concerned corporations to expedite land allocation, tendering and construction to ensure projects were completed within stipulated timelines. He also asked officials to ensure that Pumped Storage Projects (PSPs) progressed as per their targets.
 
During the meeting, Aarti Dogra, secretary of the Energy Department, briefed officials on the progress of various projects.
 
She said 28 of the state's 41 districts, covering more than 13.56 lakh farmers, were receiving electricity in two separate daytime blocks. Ajmer Discom has become the first distribution company in Rajasthan to extend the two-block supply system to all its districts, she said.
 
In the remaining four districts under Jaipur Discom — Sawai Madhopur, Kotputli-Behror, Baran and Alwar — 28 new 33 kV grid substations (GSS) are being developed to extend the two-block supply arrangement to farmers.
 
The power sector's total deficit stood at ~92,069 crore as of March 31, 2023, and rose to ~98,634 crore by December 31, 2023, an increase of ~6,565 crore, or 7.13 per cent, in nine months.
 
At an estimated annual growth rate of 9.50 per cent, the deficit would have reached ~1,21,073 crore by FY26.
 
However, measures taken by the Energy Department to contain the deficit brought the projected figure for FY26 down to Rs 89,907.77 crore. The department is continuing to expand energy capacity while maintaining financial discipline.

data.title: Tata Trusts meet: SDTT approves over ₹150 crore in grants for 5 initiatives
data.description:
The Sir Dorabji Tata Trust approved over ₹150 crore in grants to five initiatives, including ₹50 crore to a hospital in Pune led by Jehangir H C Jehangir, who has been associated with other Tata Trusts.

All the proposals at the meeting chaired by Tata Trusts chairman Noel Tata, and also attended by Venu Srinivasan and Vijay Singh, people aware of the matter said.

There was no discussion at the meeting on any of the other issues within the Tata group dominating the headlines, they said.

Amid questions raised over a grant being made to an entity with whom Jehangir, a trustee of the Sir Ratan Tata Trusts, is associated, a source asserted that there is "no conflict of interest" in this case.

 

Pune's Jehangir Hospital, which is promoted by the Cowasji Jehangir Trust counts on Jehangir HC Jehangir as the chief executive.

Senior management of the hospital made a detailed presentation at the SDTT meeting held at the Tata Trusts office in Mumbai on Thursday, where they spoke about a ₹300-crore expansion plan.

The 350-bed multispeciality hospital is expanding by constructing one more building and SDTT is supporting them with the same, they said.

A fourth of the beds at the hospital are reserved for subsidised care, they added.

The SDTT trustees felt that a hospital raising its own resources needs to be encouraged through financial support at a time when many healthcare providers are raising money from private equity players.

Other proposals discussed and passed at the meeting include proposals on a sports academy, poverty alleviation and girl child support, they said, adding that many of the projects are in backward regions.

Rest of the proposals involve grants of about ₹25-30 crore each, they said, adding that the overall grants cleared at the meeting will total to ₹150-200 crore.

To a specific question on other discussions, given that the meeting comes less than a week ahead of a crucial Tata Sons board meeting on November 26, a source said all trustees requested others to exit the room and spoke among themselves for around 10 minutes.

Other attendees at the meeting included Noel's son Neville and Tata group veteran Bhaskar Bhat, they said, adding that Srinivasan and Singh attended virtually.

In the divisions among the upper echelons of Tata group, Srinivasan and Singh have sided against Noel, while the other trustees are with him.

Bagging Jehangir's support will be crucial for Noel Tata as he navigates in the battle for Tata Sons, the holding company of the country's largest Indian conglomerate where Tata Trusts has a 65 per cent stake.

Tata Sons has not been able to hold its annual general meeting (AGM) as SRTT has been frozen by the Maharashtra charity commissioner.

At the last board meet of Tata Sons on September 17, all board members, including Srinivasan, sided against Noel on crucial votes, including chairman N Chandrasekaran's reappointment and complying with the RBI mandate for listing Tata Sons.

The Tata Education and Development Trust is also scheduled to have a meeting on Friday afternoon. The board members of this trust include Noel Tata, Mehli Mistry, and JN Mistry.

data.title: IBPS PO Mains Result 2026 today: Check steps to download PDF scorecard
data.description:
The Institute of Banking Personnel Selection (IBPS) will release the Probationary Officer (PO) Mains Result 2026 today, November 20. The IBPS PO Main exam result will be available late evening, according to information on the official website.
 
Candidates who appeared for the Common Recruitment Process for Probationary Officers/Management Trainees (CRP PO/MT-XVI) can check their results on the official website, ibps.in.

How to check IBPS PO Mains Result 2026?

Step 1: Visit the official IBPS website at ibps.in.
 
Step 2: On the homepage, press on the "CRP PO/MT" link.
 
Step 3: Click on the link that says "IBPS PO Mains Result 2026."
 
Step 4: Fill in your registration/roll number and password or date of birth.
 
 
Step 5: Enter the captcha code and click on "Login."
 
Step 6: Your IBPS PO result 2026 will display on the screen.
 
Step 7: Check your section-wise and total marks, then download the scorecard.
 
Step 8: Take a printout and keep it safe for the next phase.

Details mentioned on IBPS PO Mains Result 2026

After accessing the results, individuals should carefully examine the data shown on the results page. Candidates must check their personal details and follow the official process if they notice any error. 
 
The specifics included may vary based on the format of the document issued by IBPS, and they could consist of:
 
Candidate's name
 
Roll number and registration number
 
Examination name
 
Qualifying status
 
Marks or score details, where provided
 
Instructions regarding the subsequent recruitment stage.   
ALSO READ: UPSC CSE 2026 interview dates announced, personality tests from December 7

What after the IBPS PO Mains Result 2026?

Individuals who successfully pass the Mains exams will be invited to participate in the interview phase. The interview timetable and call letters will be published independently on the official IBPS website. 
 
Candidates are advised to commence their preparations by reviewing banking knowledge, current events, and their personal profile information. The ultimate selection will be based on the combined scores attained in both the Mains exam and the interview. 
ALSO READ: NTA UGC NET December 2026 schedule out, check subject-wise exam dates

data.title: RBI clarifies ₹10 lakh EDF threshold applies to each inward remittance
data.description:
The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has clarified that the ₹10 lakh threshold for filing an Export Declaration Form (EDF) by non-individual service exporters applies to each inward remittance, not their aggregate receipts, providing clarity on reporting requirements under the new foreign exchange framework.
 
In frequently asked questions (FAQs) issued on Friday, the central bank said service exporters other than resident individuals need to file an EDF only when the value of an individual inward remittance exceeds ₹10 lakh or its foreign currency equivalent. The declaration must be submitted before the proceeds are credited to the exporter's account.
 
The clarification follows the RBI's decision to simplify reporting requirements under the Foreign Exchange Management (Export and Import of Goods and Services) (Second Amendment) Regulations, 2026, notified on November 2 and made effective from October 1.
 
 
The RBI also clarified that service export invoices raised before October 1 will not require an EDF even if payment is received after that date. Resident individuals exporting services are exempt from filing a separate EDF; it will be deemed submitted once they provide the necessary information to their authorised dealer (AD) bank for crediting the inward remittance.
 
Authorised dealer (AD) banks cannot insist on an EDF before crediting inward remittances of up to ₹10 lakh for non-individual service exporters or any amount received by resident individuals. However, non-individual exporters receiving individual remittances exceeding the threshold must submit the declaration before the proceeds are credited.
 
The central bank also clarified that the SOFTEX form, earlier required for software exports, has been discontinued from October 1. Software exporters operating in the Domestic Tariff Area can now submit the EDF to any AD bank or the Software Technology Parks of India (STPI), while those operating from Special Economic Zones can submit it to the respective development commissioner.
 
For service exports, the EDF must generally be submitted within 30 days from the end of the month in which the invoice is raised. For services other than software, exporters can also submit the form on or before receipt of payment. AD banks may extend the deadline after examining the reasons provided by exporters.
 
On imports of services, the RBI said resident individuals and non-individual importers with invoice or contract values of up to ₹10 lakh need not furnish a separate import declaration. The information already provided to banks for processing outward remittances will suffice. However, banks must continue reporting the relevant transactions in the Export Data Processing and Monitoring System (EDPMS) and Import Data Processing and Monitoring System (IDPMS).
 
The RBI also clarified that the simplified reconciliation mechanism for transactions of up to ₹10 lakh will be determined by the original value of the shipping bill or invoice, not merely the outstanding amount. Thus, an invoice of ₹15 lakh with an outstanding balance of ₹5 lakh will not qualify for the simplified mechanism.
